questions.q: What is the new report from Scheduling, weeks after Lessons 3-12's fixes?
options: The provider-schedule lookup, fine yesterday, is now slow for some providers but not others, with no deployment
Billing's invoice lookup has started failing with an error
dbo.vw_HealthDashboard has started returning no rows ever
The Elastic Job from Lesson 11 stopped running entirely
questions.explain: dbo.usp_GetProviderSchedule is reported fine yesterday, slow today for some providers, with nothing deployed.

questions.q: What's the first step before guessing at a cause?
options: Reproduce the report exactly by timing the procedure for both a reportedly-fast and a reportedly-slow provider
Immediately rewrite dbo.usp_GetProviderSchedule
Add a new index to dbo.Appointments without checking anything first
Assume this is identical to the missing-index issue from Lesson 6
questions.explain: Confirming the symptom with real timed numbers, the same discipline used throughout this chapter, comes before any fix attempt.

questions.q: What pattern emerges when testing several providers?
options: Providers with a typical or large number of appointments are slow; one atypical, low-appointment provider is fast
Every single provider is equally slow with no variation
Only providers whose name starts with a specific letter are slow
The procedure fails with an error for every provider
questions.explain: The specific tell is that typical/large providers are slow while one small, atypical provider stays fast.

questions.q: Why doesn't "no code change" rule out a real cause?
options: Cached query plans can change for reasons unrelated to the procedure's own text, like a recompile after a statistics update
No code change means literally nothing in the system could have changed
It proves the report must be false
Stored procedures can never experience performance changes without an edit
questions.explain: A plan can change due to recompilation or a statistics update even when the procedure's text is completely untouched.

questions.q: What should you NOT do yet, at this stage?
options: Rewrite the procedure or add a speculative index before confirming the actual cause
Time the procedure for multiple different ProviderID values
Record appointment counts per provider
Treat this as a real, reproducible symptom worth investigating
questions.explain: Jumping to a fix before Lesson 14 confirms the real cause repeats the exact mistake Lesson 2 warned against.
